title: 第4章　伊斯坦布尔迎来新成员：从迁移视角概览伊斯坦布尔的历史
originalTitle: CHAPTER 4 Istanbul Meets Its New Members: An Overview of Istanbul’s History as Regards Migration

zh: 第4章　伊斯坦布尔迎来新成员：从迁移视角概览伊斯坦布尔的历史
en: CHAPTER 4 Istanbul Meets Its New Members: An Overview of Istanbul’s History as Regards Migration

zh: 本章简要回顾20世纪50年代以后伊斯坦布尔的历史，将其置于人口迁入这座城市的背景中，尤其关注自50年代开始的大规模乡村人口迁移，以及迁入者融入城市生活、老伊斯坦布尔人如何看待他们等相关议题。
en: This chapter comprises a brief history of Istanbul after the 1950s in the context of migration to the city, particularly mass rural migration starting in the 1950s, and related topics such as the migrants’ integration into urban life and old Istanbulites’ perceptions about them.

zh: 埃里克-扬·祖尔歇在《土耳其：一部现代史》开篇强调，研究历史不可避免地需要分期；他将土耳其历史中20世纪50至90年代这一时期划分为：“民主党统治时期，1950—1960年；土耳其第二共和国，1960—1980年；以及第三共和国，自1980年起”（2004，v）。本章大体采用这一分期，同时参照塔希雷·埃尔曼对土耳其非正规棚户住房（gecekondu）研究所作的分期：20世纪50至60年代；70年代至80年代初；80年代中期至90年代中期；以及90年代末（2001，984）。
en: Eric Jan Zürcher, at the beginning of his book

, accents the inevitability of periodisation while studying history, and divides the 1950s to 1990s period in Turkey’s history as follows: “the rule of the Democratic Party, 1950–60; the second Turkish Republic, 1960–80 and, the Third Republic: since 1980” (2004, v). This chapter loosely adopts this periodisation, together with Tahire Erman’s periodisation regarding studies on informal shanty housing (
) in Turkey: the 1950s and the 1960s; the 1970s and the early 1980s; the mid-1980s and the mid-1990s; and the late 1990s (2001, 984).

zh: 伊斯坦布尔从公元330年至1453年是东罗马帝国的首都，从1453年至1923年则是奥斯曼帝国的首都。18至19世纪，这座城市成为欧洲重要的商贸中心，其世界主义特征也更加鲜明（Keyder and Öncü 1993，14）。由于皇宫与帝国行政机构设在伊斯坦布尔，大批西化的上层穆斯林居住在这里，这也增添了城市的世界主义氛围。直到第一次世界大战以前，城中仍有相当数量的少数群体人口，包括希腊人、塞法迪犹太人和亚美尼亚人（14—15）。
据1885—1886年人口普查，截至1886年，在这座约有一百万人口的城市中，穆斯林土耳其人仅占44%（Toprak et al. 1997，201）。
en: Istanbul was the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire from ad 330 until 1453 and the Ottoman Empire from 1453 until 1923. As the city became an important centre of commerce and trade in Europe during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, its cosmopolitan character grew even stronger (Keyder and Öncü 1993, 14). Since the imperial palace and administration were located in Istanbul, a significant number of Westernised upper-class Muslims inhabited the city, which contributed to its cosmopolitan atmosphere. Until World War I, the city had a significant minority population comprising Greeks, Sephardic Jews and Armenians (14–15).
According to the 1885–1886 census, as of 1886, Muslim Turks constituted only 44 per cent of the city’s population which was around one million (Toprak et al. 1997, 201).

zh: 第一次世界大战之后的一系列事件，促使伊斯坦布尔的少数群体人口减少。尽管1923年希腊与土耳其之间的人口交换不包括伊斯坦布尔的希腊少数群体，但在两次世界大战之间，相当多不再觉得在这个国家安全、安稳的富裕非穆斯林家庭与外国人迁往了国外（Keyder and Öncü 1993，15）。凯末尔主义政权将安卡拉定为土耳其共和国首都后，伊斯坦布尔“成了衰颓的奥斯曼世界主义的象征性遗迹［……］，不仅在政治上，也在文化上被边缘化了”（15）。然而，第二次世界大战之后，受土耳其国际政治经济关系变化的推动，伊斯坦布尔成为扩张中的经济的“增长极”（16）。
en: A series of events following World War I provoked the minority population’s decline in Istanbul. While the 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey excluded Istanbul’s Greek minority, in the period between the World Wars a substantial number of wealthy non-Muslim families and foreigners who no longer felt safe and secure in the country emigrated (Keyder and Öncü 1993, 15). After the Kemalist regime made Ankara the capital of the Turkish Republic, Istanbul, which “became the symbolic vestige of decadent Ottoman cosmopolitanism [...] was marginalized not only politically but also culturally” (15). However, after World War II, as a result of the dynamics in Turkey’s international political and economic relations, Istanbul became the “growth pole” of the expanding economy (16).

zh: 20世纪50至60年代
en: The 1950s and the 1960s

zh: 1950至1970年间，私营制造企业在伊斯坦布尔广泛发展，“土耳其私营工业总就业人数的51%”集中于这座城市（17），由此产生了相当大的劳动力需求。此外，20世纪50年代后半期，时任总理阿德南·门德雷斯启动了一项大规模城市改造计划，给城市的历史与文化遗产造成了灾难性的影响，也将城市变成了一个巨大的工地，产生了对劳工的需求，其中包括无技能劳工。
en: Between 1950 and 1970 private manufacturing enterprises spread in Istanbul and “51 percent of total employment in Turkish private industry” was located in the city (17), which created a considerable need for labour. Additionally, in the second half of the 1950s, Adnan Menderes, the prime minister of the time, launched an extensive urban transformation project, with disastrous effects on the city’s historical and cultural heritage, which turned the city into a massive building site and created demand for labourers, including unskilled ones.

zh: 塞玛·埃尔德尔将过去与现在的伊斯坦布尔描述为“迁移人口的目的地，其人口构成不断变化，并具有世界主义特征”（1999，161）。她指出，直到20世纪50年代，城市人口都由穆斯林与少数群体组成；这些少数群体——即亚美尼亚人、希腊人和犹太人——不仅是城市中的宗教少数群体，也是族群少数群体（161）。埃尔德尔观察到，50年代以后，伊斯坦布尔人口几乎同时经历了两大变化。一方面，少数群体人口减少了。另一方面，城市迎来了两股主要迁移浪潮：受益于国际协定、来自巴尔干国家的土耳其迁入者，以及来自安纳托利亚的乡村迁入者，成为城市的新成员（161）。
en: Sema Erder describes the past and the present Istanbul as “a destination for migrant populations, changing and cosmopolitan in its composition” (1999, 161). She points out that, until the 1950s, the Muslims, and the minorities (i.e., Armenians, Greeks and Jews) who were not only the religious but also the ethnic minorities of the city, comprised the urban population (161). As Erder observes, after the 1950s Istanbul’s population went through two major changes almost simultaneously. On the one hand, the minority population declined. On the other, the city received two major waves of migration: Turkish migrants from Balkan countries benefiting from international agreements and rural migrants from Anatolia became the new members of the city (161).

zh: 城市少数群体人口减少的第一阶段，源于1942年11月征收的财富税，其征收对象是那些从战争中获利的人。财富税法的实施令人震惊：“人数较少的非穆斯林群体［……］被征收的税率，比穆斯林高十倍”（Zürcher 2004，199—200）。1955年9月6至7日发生了针对城中希腊人的骚乱，既可耻又具有破坏性，一些亚美尼亚少数群体成员也遭到袭击；再加上1964年土耳其驱逐希腊公民的事件，城市失去了相当大一部分少数群体人口。
en: The first phase of the minority population’s decline in the city resulted from the Wealth Tax imposed in November 1942 aimed at those who had profited from the war. Implementation of the Wealth Tax law was scandalous: “the small non-Muslim communities, [...] were subjected to rates ten times higher than those of Muslims” (Zürcher 2004, 199–200). With the shameful and devastating Riots of 6–7 September 1955 against the Greeks in the city, where some members of the Armenian minority were also attacked, and the 1964 expulsion of Greek citizens from Turkey the city forfeited a significant portion of its minority population.

zh: 就迁入城市而言，由于来自巴尔干的迁入者是在公共当局的监督下定居伊斯坦布尔的，因此他们被接纳并无困难。乡村迁入者则不同，他们试图自行寻找在城中生存的办法：在老城里人眼中，这些安纳托利亚迁入者是“农民”（Erder 1999，161）；老居民把“他们到来的方式、占用土地、建造住房、寻找工作以及生活方式［……］都看作异己之物”（162）。由此产生了“城市的农民化”话语，以及“城市居民—农民之分”（161）。埃尔德尔指出，被视为一个同质群体的乡村迁入者，被期望通过“改变［自身的］生活方式”来融入城市生活（162）。直到20世纪80年代，这种融入应当具有怎样的特征，始终是记者与学者热烈争论的话题；他们批评那些未能成功融入城市文化的人（162）。迁入者的融入，是城市问题讨论的焦点（162）。
en: Where migration to the city is concerned, since migrants from the Balkans had settled in Istanbul under the supervision of public authorities their reception was unproblematic, which was not the case for rural migrants who had tried to find their own ways to survive in the city: these Anatolian migrants were “peasants” in the eyes of the old urbanites of the city (Erder 1999, 161), who regarded “their mode of arrival, occupation of land, construction of housing, search for employment, and style of life [...] as alien” (162). This led to the discourse of the “peasantization of cities” and an “urban-peasant divide” (161). As Erder observes, rural migrants who were seen as a homogeneous group were expected to integrate into urban life by “changing [their] life styles” (162). Until the 1980s, the characteristics of this integration was a heated debate for journalists and scholars who criticised those who could not successfully integrate into the urban culture (162). Migrants’ integration was the focus of discussions on urban problematics (162).

zh: 大多数乡村迁入者居住在棚屋中。土耳其语中指棚屋的词是gecekondu，意为一夜之间建成。棚户聚居区在20世纪40年代末开始出现，是“那些被正规住房市场和国家双双排除在外的人所采取的一种非市场解决办法”（Işık and Pınarcıoğlu 2001，112）。在棚户现象的初期，迁入者“在城市边缘的国库土地上”搭建棚屋（113）。奥乌兹·厄舍克与梅利赫·珀纳尔哲奥卢指出，这一时期的棚户聚居区没有造成严重冲突，原因有二。第一是“多阶段迁移”（114）：迁入者得以维持与故乡的经济和社会联系，可以暂时返乡，并在自己站稳脚跟后再把家人接到城市，这减轻了迁移的创伤（115）。第二个因素是土地所有权结构。在土耳其，国家拥有城市及周边地区土地的最大份额，这些土地被称为国库土地（115）。迁移的最初阶段，迁入者占用一块块国库土地搭建棚屋时，国家选择在这一过程中保持“一名沉默的合作者”的角色（115）。厄舍克与珀纳尔哲奥卢还强调，同乡关系网络是早期棚户生活的另一个关键特征（117）。正如恰拉尔·凯德尔指出的，由于国家在实践中并未履行福利国家的职能，城中的新来者便在一定程度上通过“亲属与邻里互惠”彼此支持（2005，127）。
en: The majority of rural migrants lived in shanty houses. The word for a shanty in Turkish is

, which means built overnight. Shanty settlements started to appear by the end of the 1940s, as “a non-market solution for those who were excluded by the formal housing market as well as the state” (Işık and Pınarcıoğlu 2001, 112). In the first era of the shanty phenomenon, migrants built their shanties “on the Treasury land on the periphery of the city” (113). As Oğuz Işık and Melih Pınarcıoğlu observe, during this era, shanty settlements did not cause a serious conflict owing to two factors. The first was “

” (114) which enables the migrant to maintain his financial and social ties with his hometown and go back for a while, and bring his family to the city after he is established, which reduces the trauma of migration (115). The second factor was the structure of land ownership. In Turkey the state owns the largest share of land in and around cities, which is called the Treasury land (115). At the first stages of migration, as migrants occupied pieces of the Treasury land for building shanties, the state preferred to remain “a silent collaborator” in the process (115). Işık and Pınarcıoğlu also stress that a common hometown origin network was another key characteristic of the early era of shanty life (117). As Çağlar Keyder points out, since the state was not acting as a welfare state in practice, newcomers in the city were supporting each other to a certain extent through “kinship and neighbourhood reciprocity” (2005, 127).

zh: 埃尔曼发现，在前述四个时期，人们看待棚户居民的方式发生了显著变化。她指出，在20世纪50至60年代，他们被视为“乡村他者”（2001，984）。在那些年，人们认为他们带着乡村文化来到城市，并将其视为农民。因此，“受［现代化］理论影响，土耳其学者期望乡村迁入者被同化到现代城市社会之中”（985）。这一取向既主导了公众舆论，也主导了城市规划与组织机构。
en: Erman finds considerable changes in the way shanty dwellers were perceived in the four periods mentioned above. She asserts that in the 1950s and the 1960s they were seen as “the rural Other” (2001, 984). In those years, they were viewed as having arrived in the city with their rural culture and regarded as peasants. Thus, “under the influence of [modernisation] theory, Turkish scholars expected the assimilation of rural migrants into the modern urban society” (985). This approach dominated public opinion as well as the institutions of urban planning and organisation.

zh: 凯德尔的分析清晰地概括了20世纪50至60年代。他指出，在门德雷斯的发展主义愿景中，伊斯坦布尔被视为“国家发展的政治经济”的火车头（2010，180）。凯德尔提到，这座城市的人口“从50年代到60年代翻了一番”，其增长的特征是缺乏秩序与规划，因为“棚户区出现在最容易占地和建房的地方，［而］工业则设在最容易排污的地方”（181）。这就是20世纪60年代末的城市图景。
en: Keyder’s analysis summarises the 1950s and the 1960s in a lucid way. He acknowledges that through Menderes’s developmentalist vision Istanbul was seen as the locomotive of the “political economy of national development” (2010, 180). In the city where the population “doubled from the 1950s to the 1960s”, Keyder notes, growth was characterised by a lack of order and planning since “shantytowns developed where it was easiest to occupy and to build, [and] industry was located where it was easiest to pollute” (181). This was the picture of the city as it reached the end of the 1960s.

zh: 20世纪70年代
en: The 1970s

zh: 20世纪70年代，随着一些棚屋所有者开始出租或出售棚屋，棚屋逐渐从贫困迁入者不得已解决住房问题的办法，演变为“能够获利的商品”（Erman 2001，986）。这一时期也恰逢人们开始关注城市郊区的高档住房，进而抬高了市中心以外地区的地价。尽管如此，执政党并未对棚屋建造者采取打击行动，因为这些年正值左翼积极活动的时期，而棚户居民是左翼的潜在支持者（987）。埃尔曼补充说，在70年代至80年代初的棚户研究中，棚户居民被视为“处于不利地位的他者”（984）。
en: In the 1970s, shanties started to evolve from an inevitable solution of poor migrants to their housing problem to “profitable commodities” (Erman 2001, 986), as some shanty owners started renting or selling them. This era also coincides with the interest in upmarket housing in the suburbs of the city, which increased the value of the land outside the city centre. Despite that, the ruling parties did not act against shanty builders, as these were the years of leftist activism and shanty dwellers were potential supporters of the left (987). Erman adds that, in the 1970s and early 1980s, shanty dwellers were perceived as “the disadvantaged Other” (984) in shanty studies.

zh: 总体而言，正如埃尔德尔所解释的，在20世纪80年代之前，迁入者在城中的存在并未真正造成什么问题。迁入男性辛勤工作，工资低廉；他们的妻子则在中上阶层家庭中充当帮佣，发挥着作用。“对政治家而言，他们是可以开发的潜在票仓；对政府官员而言，他们是比公民要求更少的‘民众’”（1999，162）。然而，无论对于迁入者，还是对于老伊斯坦布尔人，城市都绝非一片乐土。凯德尔将70年代的伊斯坦布尔描述为“一座肮脏、疏于整治、昏暗的第三世界大都市”，并强调，这座城市到70年代中期已有约四百万人口，甚至上层阶级居住的区域也存在基础设施问题，建筑外立面“阴沉晦暗”（2010，181）。1974年土耳其入侵塞浦路斯后，更多希腊人离开伊斯坦布尔，进一步加重了这座城市在那个年代令人窒息的氛围。
en: Overall, until the 1980s, as Erder explains, migrants’ presence in the city did not really cause a problem. Migrant men worked hard for low wages, while their wives were useful as helpers in middle and upper-class homes. “For politicians they were a potential store of votes to be tapped, and for government officials they were ‘people’ less demanding than citizens” (1999, 162). Yet, the city was by no means a bed of roses, neither for migrants nor for the old Istanbulites. Keyder describes the Istanbul of the 1970s as “a grimy, unkempt, and dark third-world metropolis”, stressing that in the city, which had a total population of around four million inhabitants by the middle of the decade, even upper-class areas had infrastructure problems and “gloomy facades” (2010, 181). The departure of more Greeks from Istanbul as a result of Turkey’s invasion of Cyprus in 1974 added to the claustrophobic atmosphere in the city in that decade.

zh: 20世纪80年代
en: The 1980s

zh: 1980年9月12日的军事政变残酷镇压了国内的左翼运动，此后一个新政府成立了。新任总理图尔古特·厄扎尔迅速推行自由主义经济政策。埃尔曼强调，这些政策对大多数人口产生了严重的负面影响：迁往大城市的人数增加，而“失业率以及随之而来的社会不满”也不断上升（2001，987）。她补充说，那些年收入分配的变化不利于穷人，使“经济上处于不利地位的阶层，尤其是城中的乡村迁入者”越来越不满（987）。与此同时，1984至1987年的赦免法使在棚屋用地上建造最高四层的楼房获得了合法性。这导致“棚户住房的商业化；这也可以再次被解释为，政府在‘收买’那些受其自由主义政策伤害最深的人”（987）。
en: After the 12 September 1980 military coup which brutally repressed the leftist movement of the country, a new government was formed. The new Prime Minister Turgut Özal swiftly introduced liberal economic policies. Erman stresses that these policies had serious negative effects on the majority of the population: migration to large cities increased while “unemployment rates and hence social discontent” climbed (2001, 987). She adds that, as distribution of income changed to the detriment of the poor in those years, discontent accelerated among “the economically disadvantaged strata, particularly among rural migrants in the city” (987). In the meantime, the Amnesty Acts of 1984–1987 rendered it legitimate to build up to four-storey buildings on shanty land. This resulted in “the commercialization of
, which could be interpreted again as the government’s ‘bribing’ those who suffered the most for their liberal policies” (987).

zh: 随着公寓楼开始取代原来的棚屋，棚户住房失去了最初作为栖身之所的意义和功能，转而成为利润来源，因为“棚户住房的‘公寓化’变得十分普遍”（987）。不过，并非所有棚户居民都能从住房中获利。埃尔曼指出，在20世纪80年代，一些人致富了，另一些人却陷入“日益加深的匮乏”（987）。因此，她把80年代中期至90年代中期棚户研究的视角描述为：“‘城市贫民他者’与‘不应享有优待的他者’、‘作为亚文化的文化低下他者’相对立”（984）；这意味着棚户居民内部出现了分化。埃尔曼观察到，这一过程引发了新富迁入者与城市精英之间的社会文化冲突。她认为，到80至90年代，人们已清楚地看到，“乡村迁入者／棚户居民［能够］迅速跃升至较高的经济阶层”，也能够“通过创造自身的生活方式与价值体系来塑造城市”——而他们的生活方式与价值观，同“追求现代化的城市精英”的生活方式与价值观有着天壤之别（987）。一些原先的棚户居民搬进了公寓，把“自身的文化”带入新的空间（987）。埃尔曼将这一时期界定为“乡村迁入者／棚户居民”被视为“作为亚文化的文化低下他者”的阶段（987）。总之，在80年代，社会分裂呈现出比单纯的“城市居民—农民之分”更复杂、更具多重维度的形态（Erder 1999，162）。此外，从80年代中期开始，城市的面貌随着全球化进程开始改变（Keyder 2005，128），下文将考察这一现象。
en: While apartment blocks started to replace former shanties, shanty housing lost its initial meaning and function as shelter, and turned into a source of profit as “the ‘apartmentalisation’ of gecekondus became a widespread phenomenon” (987). Yet, not all shanty dwellers were able to profit from their houses. As Erman notes, in the 1980s, while some of them were becoming rich, others were suffering from “increasing deprivation” (987), hence her description of the perspective in shanty studies between the mid-1980s and the mid-1990s as “‘the urban poor Other(s)’ versus ‘the undeserving Other(s)’ and ‘the culturally inferior Other(s) as sub-culture’” (984), implying a separation between shanty dwellers. As Erman observes, this process brought forth a social and cultural clash between the newly rich migrants and the urban elites. According to her, in the 1980s and the 1990s it became clear that “rural migrants/

people [could] rapidly jump up to a higher economic stratum” and also “shape the city by creating their own ways of life and sets of values”— and there was a world of difference between their life styles and values and those of the “modernising urban elites” (987). Some former shanty dwellers moved into apartments carrying “their own culture” to their new spaces (987). Erman defines this era as the stage when “rural migrants/

people” were regarded as the “the culturally inferior Other as sub-culture” (987). In conclusion, the split in society took on a more complex and multi-dimensional form than a simple “urban-peasant divide” in the 1980s (Erder 1999, 162). Additionally, from the middle of the decade onwards the city’s face started to change in line with the process of its globalisation (Keyder 2005, 128), a phenomenon examined below.

zh: 20世纪90年代
en: The 1990s

zh: 20世纪90年代，尤其是90年代中期以后，伊斯坦布尔的社会、经济、文化和政治生活，受到三种彼此关联、又与城中迁移和迁入者密切相关的现象的深刻影响：境内流离失所的库尔德人来到伊斯坦布尔；全球化、城市贫困与社会排斥；以及政治伊斯兰的兴起。
en: Social, economic, cultural and political life in Istanbul in the 1990s, especially after the mid-1990s, was marked by three interrelated phenomena closely related to migration and migrants in the city: the arrival of internally displaced Kurds in Istanbul; globalisation, urban poverty and social exclusion; and the rise of political Islam.

zh: 自20世纪80年代起，库尔德工人党（Partiya Karkeren Kurdistan，PKK）为库尔德民族运动而与土耳其共和国交战。随着其游击袭击愈加猛烈，并演变为低烈度战争，国家开始疏散库尔德村庄，以阻止村民支持游击队。加上其他使当地生活无法忍受的政策与强制措施，估计有两百万至三百万公民在境内流离失所（Çelik 2005，980）；吉汉·艾哈迈特贝伊扎德将其描述为一种“内部离散”（2007，161）。尤其在90年代后半期，大量库尔德人从该国东部涌入大都市——主要位于西部——这不同于他们此前出于经济原因的迁移。如果我们把经济迁移视为“自愿的”，那么就可以把90年代的迁移称为“非自愿的”。贝迪兹·耶尔马兹认为，虽然这类迁移通常被称为“强迫迁移”，但“非自愿迁移”一词更为合适，因为它既包括被疏散村庄中的迁移者，也包括那些“由于与冲突环境相关的各种原因”而迁移的人（2008，135）。
en: As the guerrilla attacks of the Partiya Karkeren Kurdistan (the Kurdistan Workers Party) (PKK), fighting for the Kurdish national movement against the Turkish Republic since the 1980s, intensified and took the form of a low-intensity war, the state started to evacuate Kurdish villages in order to stop the villagers supporting the guerrillas. Together with other policies and enforcements which made life in the area unbearable, an estimated two to three million citizens were internally displaced (Çelik 2005, 980), which is described by Cihan Ahmetbeyzade as an “internal diaspora” (2007, 161). The inrush of a substantial number of Kurds from the eastern parts of the country into its (mostly western) metropolises, especially in the second half of the 1990s, was different from their earlier economic migration. If we consider economic migration as ‘voluntary’, then we can call the migration in the 1990s ‘involuntary’. Bediz Yılmaz argues that although this type of migration is usually addressed as “
”, the term “
” would be more suitable since it covers those who migrated from evacuated villages as well as those who migrated “due to various reasons connected with the conflict environment” (2008, 135).

zh: 德尼兹·于克塞凯尔列举了20世纪90年代这种境内流离失所所引发的问题：“城市贫困、无法获得教育与医疗服务、缺乏社会保障、失业，以及城市空间中的歧视”（2007，256）。原先生活在乡村、以农业和畜牧业为生的库尔德人口，由于缺乏必要的教育或工作经验，在城市中心的就业市场中没有竞争的机会。此外，与经济迁移者不同，境内流离失所的库尔德人也无法享有多阶段迁移的好处。他们的居住条件十分恶劣，无法获得足够的食物，孩子大多没有机会上学（264）。于克塞凯尔补充说，在境内流离失所的情况下，“传统的团结网络”无法发挥作用，因为多数亲属也很贫困，而且同样在境内流离失所（264）。此外，在伊斯坦布尔，搭建棚屋也不是这些库尔德人的可行选择：城中可供建房的地方已所剩无几，他们没有经济能力在这些地方搭建棚屋。因此，他们只能租住没有基础设施的棚屋，或衰败街区中的公寓。如果有机会“在流离失所之前卖掉牲畜或部分财产”，其中一些人还能买下这样的住房（265—266）。
en: Deniz Yükseker lists the problems triggered by this internal displacement in the 1990s as follows: “urban poverty, lack of access to education and health services, lack of social security, unemployment, and discrimination within urban spaces” (2007, 256). The Kurdish population living in the countryside who made their living through agriculture and stock breeding did not have the opportunity to compete in the job market in urban centres, as they did not have the necessary education or job experience. Moreover, unlike economic migrants, internally displaced Kurds did not have the benefits of multi-stage migration. Their housing conditions were very poor, they could not adequately feed themselves, and their children mostly did not have the chance to go to school (264). Yükseker adds that in the case of internal displacement “traditional solidarity networks” were not functional, as most of the relatives were also poor and they were also internally displaced (264). Additionally, building a shanty was not an option for the internally displaced Kurds in Istanbul since they did not have the financial means to build them in the few areas left in the city where this could have been possible. Thus, they either rented shanties with no infrastructure or apartments in run-down neighbourhoods. Some of them could purchase such housing if they had the opportunity to “sell their livestock or some of their property just before displacement” (265–266).

zh: 境内流离失所的库尔德人从事“非正规且不稳定的工作”，如“间歇性地做街头小贩或建筑工人”；有些人则做“季节性农业劳工”。一些儿童在街头售卖“纸巾与瓶装水”，一些女性从事“照料儿童或房屋清洁”的工作，而相当多“十几岁的女儿则在服装作坊里工作”（267—268）。收集并出售原材料，也能提供一些非正规收入（Çağlayan et al. 2011，23）。
en: Internally displaced Kurds did “informal and irregular jobs” such as “periodic work as street peddlers or as construction workers” while some of them worked as “seasonal agricultural labourers”; some children worked on the streets selling “tissue paper and bottled water”, some women worked in “childcare or housecleaning”, while a considerable number of “the teenage daughters worked in garment workshops” (267– 268). Collecting and selling raw material also provided some informal income (Çağlayan et al. 2011, 23).

zh: 许多境内流离失所的库尔德人缺乏用土耳其语交流所必需的语言能力。此外，随着公众舆论因库尔德工人党的游击战与恐怖袭击而对库尔德人日益敌视，城市中境内流离失所的库尔德人遭遇了歧视。于克塞凯尔指出，境内流离失所的后果之一，就是“在城市空间中受到歧视”，进而导致社会排斥（2007，257）。如前所述，乡村迁入者由于被污名化为农民而受到偏见；但库尔德迁入者则同时因其库尔德人身份和农民身份而遭受双重偏见（274）。哈姆扎·阿克坦强调，库尔德街区在贫困中挣扎，逐渐变得孤立；这种处境使库尔德人与土耳其人都远离了以共情为基础的共同心理立场（2012，64—65）。因此，在20世纪90年代的伊斯坦布尔，社会排斥是一个重要的社会问题。
en: Many internally displaced Kurds did not have the necessary language skills to communicate in Turkish. Additionally, as a result of the escalating hostility against Kurds in public opinion in response to the PKK’s guerrilla war and terror attacks, internally displaced Kurds in the cities experienced discrimination. As Yükseker observes, one of the results of internal displacement was “being subject to discrimination in urban spaces” which led to social exclusion (2007, 257). As discussed earlier, rural migrants faced prejudice due to stigmatisation as peasants, yet Kurdish migrants experienced a double prejudice both for being Kurdish and for being peasants (274). Hamza Aktan emphasises that as the Kurdish neighbourhoods struggled with poverty, they became isolated, a situation which pushed both Kurds and Turks away from a common mental ground based on empathy (2012, 64–65). Consequently, in the Istanbul of the 1990s, social exclusion was an important societal problem.

zh: 伊斯坦布尔的城市贫困，在20世纪80年代厄扎尔时代的新自由主义经济政策下已严重加剧；90年代，随着全球化的影响，贫困进一步增长。这导致了穷人的社会排斥，其中很大一部分是在城中境内流离失所的库尔德人。80年代以后，土耳其努力与全球化中的经济建立联系，伊斯坦布尔在这一过程中发挥了关键作用（Öncü 1997，57；Keyder 2005，124）。90年代，城市经济逐渐走向“非正规化”与“去工业化”（Keyder 2005，128）。服务业在很大程度上取代了城市中的制造业，工人阶级的劳动方式也发生了明显变化：能够加入工会的工人减少了，其中许多人甚至连“正式的社会保障安排”都没有（129）。
en: Urban poverty in Istanbul, which was seriously aggravated by the neoliberal economic policies of the Özal era in the 1980s, increased with the effects of globalisation in the 1990s. This resulted in the social exclusion of the poor, a large portion of which comprised internally displaced Kurds in the city. Istanbul had a key role in Turkey’s efforts to connect with a globalising economy after the 1980s (Öncü 1997, 57; Keyder 2005, 124). In the 1990s, the economy of the city was changing towards “informality” and “deindustrialization” (Keyder 2005, 128). The service sector mostly replaced manufacturing in the city and the modus operandi of the working class changed visibly: now fewer workers could join unions, while many of them did not even have “formal social security arrangements” (129).

zh: 凯德尔观察到，在这一过程中，新近来到城市的人已无法利用同乡与亲属关系寻找工作或建立社会联系。20世纪90年代，经济不平等加深，贫困在城市中变得清晰可见（124）。凯德尔指出，“两极分化”这个适用于第一世界全球化城市的概念，并不足以解释伊斯坦布尔这样的第三世界全球化城市的情况：这里的“两极分化”与“排斥”同时发生（128）。凯德尔将“社会排斥”定义为“在经济、政治和文化层面上社会融入的失败”，并指出，“福利体制的失灵和［……］文化融入的缺乏”是这一现象的重要催化因素（128）。
en: In this process, Keyder observes, those new to the city were not able to benefit from hometown and kinship relations in order to find jobs or make social connections. Economic inequality deepened and poverty became easily noticeable in the city in the 1990s (124). As Keyder points out, “polarisation”, a valid term for the globalising cities of the first world, is not sufficient to explain the case in the globalising cities of the third world such as Istanbul where “exclusion” is experienced concomitantly with “polarisation” (128). Keyder defines “social exclusion” as “a failure of social integration at economic, political and cultural levels”, and notes “failures in the welfare regime and [...] the lack of cultural integration” as important catalysts of this phenomenon (128).

zh: 得益于民粹主义政策，搭建棚屋的迁入者在20世纪90年代以前多少还受到公众的容忍；到了90年代，他们开始被视为“公共财产的侵占者，以及不公正特权的受益者”（130）。当搭建棚屋不再可能时，新来城市的人除租房以外别无选择，而他们负担得起的，只能是城市偏远地区或衰败街区中恶劣的住所（130）。凯德尔指出，先前官方对棚户住房的态度，使迁入者能够解决自己的住房需求；在整个发展主义时代，它是福利体制中最有效的非正规维度（131）。凯德尔准确地观察到，棚户住房及其相关机制的消失，对社会排斥的出现起到了重大作用，因为不能再建棚屋的迁入者不得不过着孤立的生活，甚至变得无家可归（131）。同样，厄舍克与珀纳尔哲奥卢认为，要理解促使土耳其城市贫困出现的动力，就需要理解“棚户现象的演变”（2001，103）。如上所述，迁移过程，以及迁入者的族群、社会、经济与文化背景，也是社会排斥出现的重要因素（Keyder 2005，131）。
en: Thanks to populist policies, migrants who built shanties were somewhat tolerated by the public until the 1990s when they started to be regarded as “invaders of public property and beneficiaries of unfair privilege” (130). In the absence of the shanty, now the newcomers to the city had no other chance than renting, and what they could afford were grim places in remote parts or in run-down neighbourhoods of the city (130). Keyder describes the former official approach to shanty housing, which enabled migrants to solve their housing needs, as the most effective of the non-formal dimensions of the welfare regime during the entire developmentalist era (131). Keyder aptly observes that the disappearance of shanty housing and related mechanisms played a major role in the emergence of social exclusion, since migrants who could not build a shanty anymore had to live in an isolated way, or even become homeless (131). Similarly, Işık and Pınarcıoğlu assert that to be able to comprehend the dynamics which led to the emergence of urban poverty in Turkey we need to understand “the evolution of the shanty phenomenon” (2001, 103). As discussed above, the migration process as well as the ethnic, social, economic and cultural background of migrants were other important factors in the emergence of social exclusion (Keyder 2005, 131).

zh: 在这样的背景下，左翼在1980年军事政变中丧失了大部分力量，已无法继续在城市边缘的棚户区或市中心贫困街区的迁入者中发挥影响。这为一种新力量的兴起铺平了道路：政治伊斯兰。正如吉汉·图阿尔所解释的，“80年代以后，伊斯兰主义政党开始吸引乡城迁入人口——部分原因在于它的社会正义议程，也在于此前承载这一议程的左翼遭到了镇压”（2009，430）。他补充说，随着地方资产阶级变得强大，并开始在大城市开展更多商业活动，“到了90年代，这个政党也获得了大都市中心的选票”（430）。图阿尔强调，这使得对伊斯兰主义者而言，“‘城市’的意涵［……］变得更为正面”；他把伊斯兰主义政党在这一阶段的议程定义为“重新征服伊斯坦布尔”（430）。在1989年的地方选举中，伊斯兰主义者赢得了伊斯坦布尔外围的两个市镇——苏丹贝伊利与阿尔纳乌特柯伊；1994年，他们的候选人R.塔伊普·埃尔多安当选伊斯坦布尔市长。图阿尔在分析这一发展对伊斯坦布尔的影响时指出，当时伊斯兰主义政党内部存在两种倾向：具有“较强新自由主义倾向”的人“主张，伊斯坦布尔在被‘征服’后，将更加融入世界”；另一些人则“希望结束那种将大众阻挡在城市边缘的精英主义排斥”（431）。他解释说，伊斯兰主义者之所以赢得棚户区的选票，源于他们善于“动员各种棚户居民网络”（431）。他还提请注意“一个新的宗教中产阶级”的出现，尽管这一群体的人数远少于棚户区居民（431）。因此，“城市逐渐伊斯兰化”（431）便不可避免了。
en: In such a context, the Left, having lost most of its power with the 1980 military coup, could no longer be influential among migrants in shanty towns on the outskirts of the city, or in the poor neighbourhoods in the city centre. This paved the way for the emergence of a new influence: political Islam. As Cihan Tuğal explains, “the Islamist party started to appeal to a rural-to-urban immigrant population after the 1980s—due in part to its social justice agenda as well as to the repression of the Left, the previous carrier of that agenda” (2009, 430). He adds that, as the provincial bourgeoisie became powerful and started to conduct more business in big cities, “in the 1990s the party also got votes from metropolitan centers” (430). Tuğal stresses that this made “the connotations of ‘the urban’ [...] to be more positive” for Islamists, and defines the agenda of the Islamist party at this stage as the “reconquest of Istanbul” (430). In the 1989 local elections, Islamists took two periphery municipalities of Istanbul, Sultanbeyli and Arnavutköy, while in 1994, their candidate R. Tayyip Erdoğan became the mayor of Istanbul. Analysing the impact of this development in the context of Istanbul, Tuğal draws attention to the fact that there were two tendencies within the Islamist party at the time: those with “more neoliberal tendencies [...] argued that after its ‘conquest’ Istanbul would be more integrated with the world”, while the others “wanted to see the termination of the elitist exclusion that had kept the masses on the borders of cities” (431). He explains that Islamists managed to win shanty votes owing to their skills “in mobilizing various kinds of squatter networks” (431). He also attracts attention to the debut of “a new religious middle class”, albeit a much smaller community than the residents of shanty towns (431). Consequently, “a gradual Islamization of cities” (431) was inevitable.

zh: 图阿尔解释说，政治伊斯兰的取向吸引了“乡城迁入者中的不同阶级”，同时也设法在某些方面帮助穷人（431）。政治伊斯兰成功地“回应了人们想在城市中找到自身位置的愿望，并表达了共同的、针对城市中心与城市精英的民粹主义反应”（431）。图阿尔指出，“两个要素对伊斯兰主义建构城市化主体至关重要：需要指引（处于‘迷失’状态），以及不同于精英”（431）。在相当大的程度上，“伊斯兰主义［……］赋予边缘聚居区和乡城迁入者一种新的认同感”（436）。图阿尔观察到，伊斯兰主义政党“培育、探索并塑造新的民众想象”；它“既塑造迁入者的身份认同与自我组织能力，也同样以这些为自身建构的基础”（436）。图阿尔强调，“当既有的迁入者身份与共同体有可能一直保持狭隘与弱小时，伊斯兰主义政治才真正介入”；他又补充说：“伊斯兰主义并不只是支持并包容迁入者的主体性与共同体，而是通过与它们互动，并重新界定它们，来改变城市”（436）。
en: Tuğal explains that political Islam’s approach appealed to various “classes within rural-to-urban immigrants”, while it managed to aid the poor in some ways (431). Political Islam managed to find “an answer to the desire to find one’s place in the city and articulating the shared populist reaction against the urban center and the urban elite” (431). Tuğal defines “two elements [which] were central to the Islamist construction of the urbanizing subject: being in need of guidance (being ‘lost’) and being different from the elite” (431). To a significant extent “Islamism [...] gives marginal settlements and rural-to-urban immigrants a new sense of identity” (436). As Tuğal observes, the Islamist party “cultivate[s], explore[s], and shape[s] the new popular imagination” while it “builds itself on the identities and self-organizing capacity of the immigrants as much as it shapes these” (436). Tuğal stresses that “Islamist politics actually comes in when existing immigrant identities and communities risk remaining parochial and weak” and adds: “Islamism, rather than simply support and include immigrants’ subjectivities and communities, transforms the city through interacting with them, but also redefining them” (436).

zh: 20世纪90年代末与21世纪最初十年
en: The Late 1990s and the 2000s

zh: 凯德尔认为，只要市政政治涉及新的城市贫困人口，就会出现“人权、平等公民身份与承认的问题”（2005，133）。他指出，90年代以后，媒体采用了一种话语，暗示棚户区中正在滋长某种动荡（133）。也是在这些年，人们开始带着贬义将棚户区称为varoş。Varoş是匈牙利语város的土耳其语形式，字面意思是城市边缘的一个街区。在土耳其，它是“一种将低收入聚居区人为界定为同质空间的标签，近年来具有强烈的排斥潜能”（Demirtaş and Şen 2007，87）。与这些变化相应，埃尔曼将90年代末棚户居民的形象描述为“具有威胁性的／varoş居民他者”（2001，984）。凯德尔指出，主流媒体把“对完整公民身份权利——公民权利、政治权利与社会权利——的诉求”，描绘为文化差异的结果；这种差异主要带有阶级意味，其次带有族群意味，并且“叠加着现代／传统之分”（2005，133）。因此，他观察到，当人们无法实现现代化时，他们就会被指责过分固守自己的传统文化与价值观，而“融入机制的缺失”（133）却不被提及。此外，处于较富裕阶层或支配地位的人制造了一种幻觉：贫困是“一种暂时性的个人问题”，通过慈善机制提供支持，就足以与之斗争（133）。
en: As Keyder asserts, “problems of human rights, equal citizenship and recognition” are experienced in municipal politics wherever the new urban poor is concerned (2005, 133). He draws attention to the fact that, after the 1990s, the media adopted a discourse hinting that a sort of unrest was growing in shanty towns (133). These were also the years when shanty towns started to be called
in a pejorative manner.
, which is the Turkish version of the Hungarian word

, literally means a neighbourhood on the periphery of the city. In Turkey, it is “a label that artificially defines low income settlements as a homogenous space and in recent years has carried a robust exclusionary potential” (Demirtaş and Şen 2007, 87). In line with these developments, Erman describes the image of people living in shanties as “the threatening/varoşlu [

dweller] Other” in the late 1990s (2001, 984). Keyder points out that the mainstream media presents “the demand for full citizenship rights (civil, political and social)” as the outcome of cultural difference with a primarily class-based and secondarily ethnic edge, “overlaid with the modern/traditional divide” (2005, 133). Therefore, as he observes, when people cannot modernise, they are blamed for holding too much onto their traditional culture and values, while the “absence of mechanisms of incorporation” (133) are not mentioned. Additionally, those who are in the richer echelons or in dominant positions create the illusion that poverty is “an individual problem of a transitory nature” and that support through charity mechanisms can be sufficient to fight against it (133).

zh: 1999年伊斯坦布尔的地震几乎终止了向这座城市的迁移（Keyder 2005，125），但全球化与新自由主义政策的影响在21世纪最初十年仍在延续。2001年2月，一场严重的经济危机导致失业大幅增加。2002年，具有伊斯兰背景、自称保守民主派的正义与发展党（AKP）组建了单一政党政府。正发党政府实施了一系列改革，“使经济融入全球资本流动网络的过程更加稳定”（Keyder 2010，182）。凯德尔认为，奉行新自由主义的正发党很清楚伊斯坦布尔的商业与投资潜力，因此政府的下一步，就是让城市为承担新角色做好准备。伊斯坦布尔既要吸引外国企业家，也要吸引游客；于是，新的豪华办公楼与住宅，以及“酒店、文化中心、会议场馆、博物馆和餐厅”陆续开业（182）。城市改造因而加速。大众住房管理局（TOKİ）想方设法，以各种各样的理由清除城市中心地区所有剩余棚屋，“例如保护遗产、缺乏防震准备、环境保护和建立绿地”（182）。这些被“修复”地区的棚户居民，发现自己被安置到了城市偏远地区由TOKİ建设的集中住房中（182）。他们因新住所遭遇严重问题，例如高额月度管理费、严格的规定与孤立处境。
en: The earthquake in Istanbul in 1999 almost ended migration to the city (Keyder 2005, 125), while the impact of globalisation and neoliberal policies continued in the 2000s. In February 2001, a major economic crisis led to a significant increase in unemployment. In 2002, Justice and Development Party (AKP), a party with Islamic origins which describes itself as conservative democratic, formed a single-party government. The AKP government carried out various reforms “which made the integration of the economy into global networks of capital flows more stable” (Keyder 2010, 182). According to Keyder, the neoliberal AKP was well aware of Istanbul’s potential for business and investment, so the government’s next step was preparing the city for its new role. Istanbul was to attract foreign entrepreneurs as well as tourists; thus, new glamorous offices and residences, as well as “hotels, cultural centers, congress venues, museums and restaurants”, were being opened (182). Consequently, the urban transformation of the city accelerated. The Mass Housing Administration (TOKİ) found ways to clear away all remaining shanties in the central parts of the city with a wide scale of excuses “such as protection of heritage, absence of earthquake preparedness, environment and creation of green zones” (182). Residents of shanties in these “rehabilitated” areas found themselves in the mass housing of TOKİ in remote parts of the city (182). They suffered from serious problems related to their new residences, such as high monthly maintenance charges, strict rules and isolation.

zh: 随着旧街区成为投资者觊觎的对象，绅士化在城市全球化过程中成为一个重要议题（183—184）。与此同时，伊斯坦布尔的历史地标、美食以及不断发展的文化生活，开始受到世界各地越来越多的关注（184）。对外国游客而言，这是一座新兴的时髦城市；对国际企业家而言，这是一片沃土。
en: Gentrification became an important issue in the city during its globalisation as old neighbourhoods turned into objects of desire for investors (183–184). Meanwhile, Istanbul’s historical landmarks, cuisine and expanding cultural life started to receive increasing interest from all over the world (184). It was the new hip city for foreign travellers and a fertile land for international entrepreneurs.

zh: 如导论所述，对旧伊斯坦布尔的怀旧，是20世纪90年代日益兴盛的一种现象。凯德尔指出，像其他竞相成为全球城市的城市一样，伊斯坦布尔必须推介自身的历史遗产。古典主义者希望强调伊斯坦布尔的拜占庭身份，而认同伊斯兰主义文化的人，则倾向于将其呈现为“许诺给信徒的［……］虔诚者的伊斯兰之城”（185）。最终，世俗精英与具有伊斯兰主义倾向的人找到了共同点：“多种文化汇聚的奥斯曼首都”（185）。这种对伊斯坦布尔作为奥斯曼首都所具有的世界主义面貌的强调，催生了一股“极其流行的怀旧潮流，以某种理想化的19世纪末伊斯坦布尔形象为参照”；它出现在“小说、文章、学术项目，以及伊斯坦布尔人的日常话语中”（Örs 2002，134）。伊莱·厄尔斯强调，随着乡村迁入者到来，城市社会结构发生变化；作为对此的回应，人们开始“向往一种理想化的多元文化共存状态”，以及这种状态的象征（135）。如第1章所述，厄尔斯将其称为“世界主义怀旧”（2018，174）。里法特·巴利尤其通过大众媒体中的表现形式来追踪这种怀旧话语；他准确指出，90年代有相当多记者认为伊斯坦布尔已经失去了自身的特征与身份，并在写作中哀悼其少数群体遗产（2002，142）。
en: Nostalgia for old Istanbul, as discussed in the Introduction, was a growing phenomenon in the 1990s. Keyder points out that Istanbul, like other cities competing to become global, had to promote its historical heritage. While the classicists wanted to emphasise Istanbul’s Byzantine identity, those sympathetic with the Islamist culture preferred to present it as “the Islamic city of the devout [...] promised to the believers” (185). Eventually, the secular elite and those with Islamist leanings found a common ground: “the Ottoman capital of many cultures” (185). This emphasis on the cosmopolitan aspect of Istanbul as the Ottoman capital resulted in an “exceedingly popular trend of nostalgia tak[ing] as its reference point a certain idealized representation of Istanbul in the late 19th century” which appears in “novels, articles and scholarly projects, and in the everyday discourse of Istanbulites” (Örs 2002, 134). İlay Örs emphasises that “a yearning towards an idealized multicultural coexistence” and its symbols emerged as a reaction to the changes in the city’s social fabric, concomitant with the arrival of rural migrants (135). As mentioned in Chapter 1, Örs describes this as “cosmopolitanist nostalgia” (2018, 174). Rıfat Bali, tracking the nostalgic discourse particularly through its manifestations in the popular media, aptly observes that in the 1990s there was a considerable number of journalists who thought that Istanbul had lost its character and identity, and lamented its minority heritage in their writings (2002, 142).

zh: 这种怀旧所涵盖的，不仅是奥斯曼时期的伊斯坦布尔，也包括大规模乡村迁移发生之前共和国早期的伊斯坦布尔；因此，它忽视了一个事实：实际上，从1923年土耳其共和国建立，到50年代乡村迁入者到来之前，少数群体人口就已经在减少。换言之，持这种话语的人，将具有世界主义特征的少数群体的消失，与乡村迁入者在城中的出现并置，从而制造了一种幻觉，仿佛是这些乡村迁入者挤走了伊斯坦布尔的少数群体，为自己腾出空间。少数群体原先居住的街区，在原有居民离开之后日渐衰败；迁入者租住其中破旧的公寓，又在潜意识层面促使人们把少数群体消失与乡村迁入者到来之间这种虚幻的关联，当作现实来接受。
en: Since this nostalgia covers not only the Ottoman but also the early Republican Istanbul before mass rural migration, it ignores the fact that the minority population had in fact declined from the establishment of the Turkish Republic in 1923 until the rural migrants’ arrival in the 1950s. In other words, as those who adopt this discourse juxtapose the disappearance of the cosmopolitan minorities with the appearance of rural migrants in the city so do they create the illusion that these rural migrants pushed out Istanbul’s minorities to make space for themselves. Migrants’ rental of run-down apartments in former minority neighbourhoods, which had been dilapidating since they were vacated by their original residents who were the members of the minority population, subliminally motivate people to accept this illusory correlation between the disappearance of minorities and the arrival of rural migrants as reality.

zh: 2010年及其后
en: The Year 2010 and After

zh: “伊斯坦布尔2010——欧洲文化之都”的庆祝活动，使伊斯坦布尔全球化的成果达到顶峰。阿苏·阿克索伊指出，在筹备庆祝活动时，2010倡议小组曾对绅士化给较低社会经济阶层带来的负面影响表示关切（2012，94）。阿克索伊补充说，城市历史区域中的改造活动，造成了文化遗产的损害（95）。那些有争议的城市改造项目，尤其是苏卢库莱与塔尔拉巴舍的项目，引发了激烈争论。由于这些项目，罗姆人在苏卢库莱失去了家园。塔尔拉巴舍也经历了相似的过程：这个原先的希腊人街区，居住着罗姆人、库尔德人，以及没有居留许可的非洲迁入者（105）。改造始于2005年，并在2010年产生了实际影响，结果是塔尔拉巴舍的大多数公寓被腾空。与此同时，费内尔、巴拉特与艾万萨赖这些历史街区于2006年启动了一项更新计划。除这些历史悠久的中心地区以外，城市外围的棚户区，如菲基尔泰佩与阿亚兹玛，也开展了城市改造活动，以腾出土地用于大规模封闭式住宅社区项目。
en: The outcome of Istanbul’s globalisation peaked with the celebration of Istanbul 2010—European Capital of Culture. As Asu Aksoy points out, the 2010 Initiative Group expressed concern about the negative impact of gentrification on the lower socioeconomic strata during the preparations for the celebrations (2012, 94). Aksoy adds that cultural heritage was damaged as a result of the urban transformation activities in the historic areas of the city (95). Controversial urban transformation projects, particularly those carried out in Sulukule and Tarlabaşı, have been the subject of fierce debate. As a result of these projects, the Romani people lost their homes in Sulukule. A similar process was experienced in Tarlabaşı, a former Greek neighbourhood, where Romani and Kurdish people as well as African migrants without residence permits lived (105). As a consequence of the transformation which began in 2005, and took effect in 2010, most of the apartments in Tarlabaşı got emptied. In the meantime, a renewal project in the historic neighbourhoods of Fener, Balat and Ayvansaray was launched in 2006. In addition to these historic central areas, urban transformation activities were conducted in shanty towns on the outskirts of the city, such as Fikirtepe and Ayazma, to make their land available for massive gated community projects.

zh: 随着全球化的发展，土耳其早在20世纪80年代就开始接纳外国移民，“其迁移格局从60至70年代大规模人口迁出，转变为90年代及21世纪最初十年广泛的人口迁入”（İçduygu 2014，9）。艾哈迈德·伊奇杜伊古解释说，“21世纪最初十年的前半段，出现了四种不同类别的移民流动：（1）非正规劳工移民；（2）过境移民；（3）寻求庇护者与难民；（4）正规移民”（5）。不出所料，土耳其的大多数外国移民居住在伊斯坦布尔。随着叙利亚内战爆发，叙利亚难民自2011年4月起逃往土耳其，进入土耳其的国际迁移在性质和规模上都发生了剧烈变化。据联合国难民署2020年10月的情况更新，土耳其境内生活着约“400万难民和寻求庇护者，其中包括超过360万叙利亚国民，以及近33万其他国籍的登记难民和寻求庇护者”（UNHCR 2020，1）。截至2020年10月，难民与寻求庇护者援助和团结协会（RASAS）援引土耳其内政部公布的官方数字表示，在伊斯坦布尔登记的叙利亚难民约有五十万人，相当于该市人口的3.3%（RASAS 2020）。
en: In relation to globalisation, Turkey started to receive foreign migrants as early as the 1980s, and “its migration profile has changed from the massive emigration of the 1960s and 1970s to extensive immigration during the 1990s and 2000s” (İçduygu 2014, 9). As Ahmet İçduygu explains, “the first part of the 2000s has witnessed immigration flows from four different categories: (1) irregular labour migrants; (2) transit migrants; (3) asylum seekers and refugees and (4) regular migrants” (5). Unsurprisingly, the majority of the foreign migrants in Turkey resided in Istanbul. The nature and size of the international migration to Turkey changed drastically with the Syrian Civil War as Syrian refugees started to flee to Turkey from April 2011 onwards. According to the UN Refugee Agency’s October 2020 update, around “4 million Refugees and asylum-seekers in Turkey including over 3.6 million Syrian nationals and close to 330,000 registered refugees and asylum-seekers of other nationalities” are living in Turkey (UNHCR 2020, 1). As of October 2020, RASAS (Refugees and Asylum Seekers Assistance and Solidarity Association), referring to the official numbers declared by the Turkish Ministry of the Interior, announced the number of registered Syrian refugees in Istanbul as around half a million which corresponds to 3.3% of the city’s population (RASAS 2020).

zh: 作为一座新兴全球城市，伊斯坦布尔不断上升的受欢迎程度，在2010年代前半期一直持续。然而，2016年的多起恐怖袭击，以及同年7月15日的未遂军事政变，使这座城市作为旅游与投资中心的吸引力骤然下降。经历四年没有恐怖袭击的和平时期之后，这一下行趋势走到了尽头；在连续二十五年由保守派市长执政之后，社会民主派的埃克雷姆·伊马姆奥卢当选市长，又带来了一丝积极气氛。因此，这座城市带着对恢复自身形象与吸引潜力的一定乐观情绪，进入了21世纪的第二个十年。
en: Istanbul’s rising popularity as an emerging global city lasted throughout the first half of the 2010s. However, various terror attacks in 2016 as well as the 15 July military coup attempt in the same year resulted in a sudden decline in the city’s attractiveness as a centre of tourism and investment. After four peaceful years free of terror attacks this downward trend came to an end, and a touch of positivity was added with the election of a social democrat mayor, Ekrem İmamoğlu, after twenty-five years with conservative mayors. Thus, the city entered the second decade of the 2000s with a degree of optimism about recovering its image and attraction potential.
body.review: 本段末句原文为“the second decade of the 2000s”，按原文译出；但上文已述及2016年及其后四年的情况，年代衔接存在疑点。此处保留底本，不擅自改为2020年代。所有“目前”等时间表述均对应作者写作时点。
